messages:
chore: run the TypeScript sources on Node's type stripping

`npm test` was `node --test` with nothing to run it against: no
dependencies, no build script and no way to type-check. Node 22 strips
types on the fly, so the tests can run against the sources directly.

Type stripping does not rewrite import specifiers, so neighbours are
imported as `./x.ts`; `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` turns those back
into `.js` on emit, and `erasableSyntaxOnly` plus `verbatimModuleSyntax`
keep the sources to syntax Node can erase. `tsconfig.test.json` checks
the tests too, which the build config cannot: it keeps them out of
`dist/`.

Adds the `typecheck` and `build` scripts, and `typescript` and
`@types/node` as devDependencies; the library keeps no runtime
dependency.

See dl-003.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: resolve JSON Pointers against a JSON document (RFC 6901)

`resolvePointer(document, pointer)` returns the value a JSON Pointer
refers to, by reference, without modifying the document. It validates
the pointer against the section 3 grammar first, then walks the document
by the section 4 rules.

It throws rather than returning a fallback, because a JSON document may
hold `null` and "no value there" must not be confused with it:
`InvalidPointerError` when the string is not a JSON Pointer,
`PointerResolutionError` when it does not resolve. Both derive from
`JsonPointerError`.

The RFC is read strictly, so that a pointer means the same thing in
every service that imports the toolkit: the URI fragment form of
section 6 is rejected, `-` on an array never resolves, array indices
must match `array-index`, and member lookup considers own members only,
so `/toString` and `/__proto__` lead nowhere.

`JsonValue` and friends are exported as the shared data model for the
building blocks to come.

See dl-001, dl-002, task-001.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
